title: Validate source-aligned padding models on independent genres and marker regimes
statement: A new descriptive work pair uses the oration in Erasmus’s Encomium artis medicae for fitting and the separate De tribus habitaculis for evaluation, removing bracketed editorial notes. Three contiguous 16-block validation folds within 64 training blocks select source order three; refit on all 64 and evaluate the first 40 blocks of the other work. For each transformed stream fit two state-specific models with exactly the same alphabet, additive 0.5 base and nested context interpolation mass 2: one sees at most three preceding output symbols, the other sees the last three source symbols and their emitted markers. The state after an emitted source letter is known to require a marker; after a marker or space the next event is source. With distinct B/D symbols and the shared rule, this alignment costs zero extra bits. Constant-marker padding costs 3.2630 versus 2.9126 bits per original symbol for output versus source context; deterministic B/D padding costs 3.2160 versus 2.9128. The unexpanded known-inverse source model costs 2.9083. For three random-permutation marker realizations, the output-context rates are 4.1188, 4.1401, 4.1099 and source-context rates 4.1000, 4.1209, 4.0962, while the source-plus-per-block combinatorial-marker inverse benchmark is 3.6786. Results include symbol counts and total bits. All outputs round-trip. This supports a context-length effect in this fixed-state family, not an information-theoretic advantage: state, rules, source/marker alphabets and block boundaries are given to encoder and decoder.
check: Repeat the frozen comparison on additional independently authored works and languages with editorial boundaries verified and multiple document-level folds. Quantify variation across documents, random marker draws and context orders; report both total code lengths and both symbol denominators. Separately transmit model parameters, transform identity, alphabet and block delimiters whenever they are not shared. Test colliding source and marker alphabets with an explicit parsable alignment code, and compare suffix padding with a decoder-computable boundary state. Do not infer joint information loss from finite-context predictive rates.

methods.inputs: Pinned PG 16561 Erasmus training, after marker Quo saepius est ars medicinae through Dixi; PG 38708 De tribus habitaculis evaluation, from Tria sunt through Gutenberg end. Bracketed notes removed then project Latin normalizer. Text attribution and normalizing choices follow pin metadata; genres and periods differ. These are new works relative to the previous three pairs, not new languages.
methods.matching: Each model predicts source and marker events separately using the same state-specific base and context interpolation. Context form is the only difference: suffix of emitted symbols versus suffix beginning at the third most recent source symbol, including intervening markers. At block starts shorter contexts are reused at higher orders in both variants. Training model tables are shared with decoder, not paid for.
methods.folds: Each of first three consecutive 16-block windows validates against the other 48 of the first 64 training blocks; choose 0–8 by summed validation bits, then fit all 64. Folds overlap in training and do not quantify independent-work uncertainty.
methods.random: Seeds 1–3 independently shuffle the same deterministic B/D marker histogram per block, with separate train and evaluation seeds. Inverse benchmark codes the recovered source plus sum log2 binomial(n,k) for each block. Other deterministic-transform seeds reproduce identical output.
methods.limits: One pair and three random realizations, not confirmatory corpus-level power. Original reference model uses its own source-alphabet interpolation and does not pay model cost. Texts and rules are assumed shared; actual compression and collisions remain untested.

reproduction.instruction: Extract extract_works.py, battery.py and transforms.py from P-J-011/mubadala777/step.json reproduction.scripts into one scratch directory. Add this script and run with the repository root and scratch directory on PYTHONPATH after fetching pinned inputs.
